question.problem:
Determine if the matrix
$A=[\begin{aligned}4 & 8 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}]$
is diagonalizable or not, and if it is diagonalizable, find a corresponding diagonal matrix $D.$
question.worked_solution:
Since $A$ is triangular, the eigenvalues are the entries on the main diagonal. 

So, the eigenvalues are ${\lambda }_{1}={\lambda }_{2}=4.$ Since we get one repeated eigenvalue, the matrix might not be diagonalizable. To check this, we row-reduce the matrix $(A-4I)\text{x}=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A-4I & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 8 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}]-4[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 8 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has only $1$ pivot column. This implies that we will have only $2-1=1$ linearly independent eigenvector corresponding to the current eigenvalue. Therefore, $A$ is not diagonalizable.
